bullets.title: AI capex fears + geopolitical risk drive broad pre-market selloff
bullets.body: Nasdaq futures -1.6% and S&P -1.0% pre-market as mixed mega-cap earnings (META/TSLA capex cuts, LRCX guide miss) collide with Iran kinetic-risk chatter and AI trade sustainability concerns. Hyperscaler credit spreads retested July wides (154bp), with CoreWeave leading HY AI basket wider; retail flows at 16th percentile with rotation out of Mag 7.

bullets.title: META beats Q3/Q4 but reverses +5% gain to -2% on equity raise overhang
bullets.body: META Q3 revenue $64.6B (+26% Y/Y) and Q4 guide $73-76B (2-pt FXN acceleration vs consensus) beat handily, with Muse hitting >10M UCAN users and 25% daily shopping engagement. However, FY26 capex raised to $135-145B (+88-101% Y/Y), a new Class C share structure (effective Jan 2027) signals equity raise 'early 2027 at hundreds of billions scale,' and FY27 opex guide absent — collectively reversed post-earnings gains. Consensus Buy at 90%; average PT ~$828.

bullets.title: LRCX record results but Dec-Q guide misses elevated bar; CY27 WFE >$200B
bullets.body: Lam Research posted modest F1Q beats but the F2Q revenue guide came in below buyside expectations, partly due to gas delivery subsystem shortages that could cost $300M+ in Dec-Q revenue. CY26 WFE raised to mid-$150B; management gave preliminary CY27 WFE >$200B (+28% Y/Y) led by DRAM, leading-edge foundry, and NAND — but supply/cleanroom constraints may shift demand to 2028. Stock down ~7-8%; Citi views it as a buying opportunity at ~15-16x C2028E.

bullets.title: TXN blowout quarter: Industrial +40% YoY, Data Center nearly doubled; CY27 pricing tailwinds building
bullets.body: Texas Instruments posted Sep-Q revenue $6.06B (+2% beat) with gross margin 64.2% vs Street 61.6% and EPS $2.62 vs $2.41. Dec-Q guide $5.80-6.30B midpoint +5% above consensus — extending above-seasonal growth to 10 consecutive quarters — driven by Industrial, Auto, and Data Center. CY27 analog pricing negotiations are ongoing, with large contract customers (auto ~30% of revenue) still in discussions; capex likely toward high end of $2-3B in 2026.

bullets.title: TSLA beats EPS but capex cut to $20B from $25B spooks AI infrastructure complex
bullets.body: Tesla Q3 EPS $0.48 beat $0.42 consensus with auto gross margin ex-credits 18.1% vs 16.3% forecast; FSD attach >75% in North America and Cybercab autonomous miles up 8x Q/Q to 2M cumulative. The capex guidance reduction to ~$20B (from >$25B) reverberated negatively through the AI/semiconductor complex. Musk separately confirmed Tesla-SpaceX merger discussions.

bullets.title: Semiconductor sector broadly lower pre-market; SOXX -3.6%; AI infrastructure names down 3-5%
bullets.body: Beyond LRCX (-8%) and TXN (relatively resilient), the broader semi complex is under pressure: SOXX -3.6%, quantum names (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) -3.5-4%, AI infrastructure (BTDR, IREN, CRWV, NBIS) -3-5%, and nuclear/clean energy (SMR, OKLO, NNE) -3-4%. Hedgeye notes semis had been overbought after a 4600%+ SNDK rally into summer peak, and NYSE/NASDAQ new lows have exceeded new highs for 37-38 consecutive days — historically an 18%+ Nasdaq decline precursor in 78% of instances.

bullets.title: Treasury yields moving sharply: 10-year at 5.04%, 2-year down 9bps to 4.73%
bullets.body: Despite equity weakness, Treasuries are rallying (haven demand), with the 2-year down ~9bps to 4.73% and 10-year up to 5.04% intraday per pre-market data — a notable divergence driven by AI-trade doubts and geopolitical risk. French 10-year at 5.1% (24-year high) and European government CDS spreads rising signal broader credit stress. JPMorgan expects $211B in Treasury supply ($69B 2yr, $70B 5yr, $44B 7yr) unchanged from last month.

bullets.title: Geopolitical escalation: Iran strike risk + Houthi attacks push WTI toward $100
bullets.body: WTI crude up ~1.8-2% to ~$99.44 on reports US/Israel are preparing renewed Iran strikes post-election, with Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continuing. Risk aversion is evident across Asian markets (Hang Seng down >3 standard deviations, KOSPI -3.5%), with safe-haven currencies (yen, Swiss franc) strengthening. GS notes geopolitical tensions are a co-driver alongside AI capex concerns in the broad market selloff.

bullets.title: META capex AI self-funding: ad revenue +26% suggests buildout economics viable
bullets.body: JPM notes META's core advertising revenue grew +26% Y/Y in Q3 and is guided +22-27% Y/Y in Q4, implying the $135-145B AI capex is 'self-funding' from the core business. Reality Labs losses are expected to narrow to $18-19B in 2026 and ~$15B in 2027, trending toward profitability. META AI Business Assistant driving ~5% higher conversions; 10M+ advertisers using generative AI features.

bullets.title: AI midterm election risk limited; Texas governor race is primary data center policy threat
bullets.body: Wolfe Research argues US midterm elections are unlikely to derail AI data center buildout — data center pipeline has more than doubled since last year, suspensions remain flat, and AI ranks 11th of 16 voter issues. The Texas gubernatorial race (Abbott with 4-pt lead but Polymarket odds eroding) is the most acute risk; TCEQ shut its permit portal to enforce a governor's order halting new data center permits, though even a Hinojosa upset wouldn't mean a permanent ban.

bullets.title: 3Q26 earnings season: 77% beat rate, +5.5% aggregate upside; TECH+ EPS growth 47.9%
bullets.body: With 21.4% of S&P 500 market cap reported, 77% of companies are beating estimates by an aggregate 5.5%. TECH+ EPS growth is tracking 47.9% Y/Y vs 27.8% for the broad market; Energy is the only other sector outpacing the index at 132.4%. The next five trading days bring 24.2% more S&P 500 market cap reporting.

bullets.title: Broad AI trade unwind: Rotation from Mag 7 into broader AI complex; NeoCloud funding concerns
bullets.body: JPM notes retail flows are subdued (16th percentile) with rotation from Mag 7 into broader AI complex and semis ex-Mag 7. CRWV is down ~30% MTD on overcapacity concerns for NeoClouds and vulnerability to debt-funded growth in a rising-rate environment. DeepSeek raising $15B (CATL and Tencent among investors) adds competitive pressure on US AI labs. Hedgeye categorizes CRWV/NBIS/IREN as 'funding bubble layer plays.'

bullets.title: SPOT Q3 solid; 4Q gross margin guide beats, premium subs +6M vs 5M guide
bullets.body: Spotify Q3 gross margin 33.0% (+136bps Y/Y), premium net adds 6M vs 5M guide (306M total), and 4Q operating income guide €820M beats consensus €773-804M. 4Q GM guide 33.8% (+80bps Q/Q) is the key beat vs feared compression from audiobook/AI investments. Revenue guided 14% FXN growth; 2027 framed as monetization year. Stock +5-6% pre-market.

bullets.title: GOOGL Search trends weakening into quarter-end; RDDT-GOOGL deal renewal at risk
bullets.body: JPM channel checks indicate Google Search growth slowed at quarter end, with a ~1-point revenue miss expected. Separately, RDDT's $60M annual data licensing deal with Google faces renewal uncertainty, with investor expectations for renewal 'down very low.' Hedgeye flags GOOGL as breaking to bearish trend.

bullets.title: P&G 1Q beat on +4% organic growth but guides cautiously; $1.4B commodity headwind in FY27
bullets.body: P&G beat 1Q EPS ($2.00 vs $1.89 consensus) on 4% organic sales growth (all segments upside), but maintained conservative FY27 guidance of +1-3% organic growth despite the strong start. Incremental commodity cost headwind of $400M after-tax raises total FY27 raw material drag to $1.4B. Stock up ~2.4%.

bullets.title: MU HBM4 in high-volume manufacturing; NAND G11 targeting 2x bit density in 2H27
bullets.body: Micron disclosed HBM4 is in high-volume manufacturing with HBM4E samples shipping; NAND strategy skips G10 to jump to G11 targeting 2H27 ramp with 2x bit density, 1.5x faster I/O, and >25% lower energy transfer. Memory remains the leading driver in LRCX's CY27 WFE outlook alongside leading-edge foundry.

bullets.title: CME upgraded to OW at JPM on rates environment; rates volumes up 19.2% QTD
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded CME to Overweight with a $367 Dec-27 PT (24% upside), applying 25x 2028E EPS (1-turn premium to 10-year avg) on the view that the hiking cycle supports incremental rates trading revenue of $222M. CME 3Q26 EPS $3.02 beat Street $2.99; rates volumes up 19.2% QTD vs Q4 2025; buybacks >$500M/quarter.

bullets.title: Celsius Consumer spending decelerated: JPM Chase data shows October MTD at ~5.9% Y/Y vs 6.8% in September
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Chase spend data shows October total spending growth (through Oct 14) decelerated to ~5.9% Y/Y from 6.8% in September, with discretionary lagging non-discretionary. This follows LVS's Q3 miss on Macau/Singapore VIP weakness and broader caution on high-end consumer spending internationally.

bullets.title: NFLX downgraded to peer perform at Wolfe; bears see '27 revenue guide risk
bullets.body: Wolfe Research downgraded Netflix to peer perform from outperform (analyst Peter Supino). Separately, Jefferies notes bears expect '27 revenue guide to come in below Street and flags potential deal-making needs. Stock at $65.04 at time of downgrade.

bullets.title: Korean KOSPI -3.5%, Hang Seng -3 std dev; Asia hedge fund de-grossing accelerates
bullets.body: Asia risk assets are in sharp selloff: KOSPI down 3.5%, Hang Seng moving more than 3 standard deviations lower, with China's CSI 300 entering bear territory on weak consumption and AI profitability concerns. UBS tech notes global risk-off tone with NDX -1.66% and hedge fund de-grossing identified as the major culprit in Asia tech selling.
